title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria
abstract: arXiv:2611.06504v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multilingual benchmarks for African languages mostly translate generic questions into local languages, measuring linguistic competence but not whether models know facts about Africa. We introduce \naija, a benchmark of factual and statistical questions about Nigeria, authored by native speakers and grounded in authoritative official statistics, with every question available in English, Nigerian Pidgin, \yoruba, Igbo, and Hausa. Answering similar questions for the UK and US yields a country by language matrix that disentangles a language effect (the model knows the fact but degrades in a low-resource language) from a knowledge effect (the fact is absent in every language). Across eight frontier and Nigeria-adapted models, the knowledge effect dominates: English-query accuracy is 49--50\% for the US/UK but 20\% for Nigeria. translated_title: NaijaFacts：一个将语言与知识从关于尼日利亚的事实中分离出来的框架
translated_abstract: 面向非洲语言的多语言基准测试大多是将通用问题翻译成当地语言，衡量的是语言能力，而非模型是否了解关于非洲的事实。我们提出了NaijaFacts，这是一个关于尼日利亚的事实性和统计性问题基准，由母语者撰写，并基于权威的官方统计数据，每个问题都有英语、尼日利亚皮钦语、约鲁巴语、伊博语和豪萨语版本。通过让模型回答针对英国和美国的类似问题，我们构建了一个国家×语言的矩阵，从而将语言效应（模型知道该事实，但在低资源语言中性能下降）与知识效应（该事实在任何语言中都不存在）分离开来。在八个前沿模型和尼日利亚适配模型上，知识效应占主导地位：以英语提问时，针对美国/英国的准确率为49%–50%，而针对尼日利亚仅为20%。语言效应较小且与网络表征程度相关，从英语到约鲁巴语逐渐下降（在尼日利亚问题上下降9个百分点）……
tldr: 该论文提出NaijaFacts基准，通过国家×语言矩阵将语言效应与知识效应分离，发现大语言模型对尼日利亚事实的知识缺口（英语提问准确率仅20%）远大于低资源语言带来的语言效应。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces NaijaFacts, a benchmark that disentangles language effects from knowledge effects via a country-by-language matrix, revealing that LLMs' knowledge gap about Nigeria (only 20% accuracy in English) dominates over the smaller language effect from low-resource languages.
